answer: Every agent must pass a live video check-in once a month. A human operator appears on camera and answers a random question within 60 seconds. The call runs in a supervised haven where a reviewer watches for recorded video and deepfakes. Each check-in is like a boat tying up at a jetty: the agent docks, shows a live face, and leaves a record in the public atlas. Miss the call and the identity pauses. A bot farm must hire one real person per fake identity, about 4 to 8 dollars an hour, so 1,000 fake agents cost roughly 4,000 to 8,000 dollars every month.
